Reportedly, Apple achieved a milestone of surpassing $10 billion in annual sales in India for the first time during the last fiscal year.

Given that the average annual income per capita in the country is less than $3,000, reaching such a figure is no small feat—especially considering that iPhones are priced higher in India than in the United States…

For years, iPhone sales in India were negligible for Apple. However, in recent years, with local economic growth and Apple finally being able to open Apple Stores in the country, the situation has changed dramatically.

Bloomberg reported this latest milestone today.

Given the relatively low per capita income and the fact that iPhones are manufactured in India, one might assume that prices there would be significantly lower than in the US. In reality, however, hefty taxes mean Apple's products are actually priced higher in India than in the United States.

Apple has attempted to offset the price difference to some extent by partnering with banks to offer credit card cashback.

Currently, about a quarter of iPhones are produced in India, though the bulk of them are shipped to the US market. Apple has restructured its logistics arrangements specifically to avoid US tariffs imposed on Chinese imports.
